endorsements.quote: User-centred design feedback loop : Incorporate human-computer interaction factors feedback from diverse users to ensure AI systems meet the needs of both users of various clinical and technological experience levels.
Employ mixed methods approaches to measure key factors such as explainability and trust.
Ultimately, when well-calibrated human-computer alignment is achieved in a pre-clinical setting, it must be further calibrated against real-world clinical and patientreported outcomes.
Provide clear metrics (e.g. input similarity or output con fidence) and explanations (e.g. saliency maps) to pro mote well-calibrated human-AI alignment.

unlisted_practices: Measure human-computer interaction factors such as trust, explainability, and workload throughout the entire life cycle of an AI innovation using validated scales and frameworks such as IDEAL and DECIDE-AI.
Design HCI evaluation in conjunction with a human-computer interaction or human factors specialist.
Balance additional explanatory information in real-time AI applications against cognitive workload and safety metrics such as distraction and workflow disruption.
Study clinician trust in AI longitudinally over time to map trust trajectories.
Incorporate dedicated HCI teams into early-stage AI analysis.

screen.reason: This is a commentary discussing human-computer interaction factors (trust, explainability) and arguing for structured evaluation frameworks for AI integration into surgical practice.
